---
title: "F100 to F110 laser migration fixture"
---

This disposable native case qualifies the MIR5 F100 `laser-turret-speed-8` to F110 `laser-shooting-speed-8` identity and `laser-turret` to `laser` native effect-category boundary. It is not a published MIR4 source or full historical compatibility campaign.

Compose each role's five files with the three shared files as `fixture_control.lua`, `fixture_data_final.lua` and `fixture_settings.lua`. Both roles select the shipped laser settings: cost1, growth1, time1, effect1% and maximum12. The data preflight checks the exact resulting row, science, prerequisites and native effect without mutating prototypes.

The source must run on exact1.0.0, earn one real laser level, freeze its lab, retain current laser research at42% with a queued braking probe, retain a separate force's27% suspended laser investment and preserve a foreign disabled/hidden laser with its42% braking queue. Save and cold reload twice. Record the source hash before preparing the successor profile.

The successor must use that exact protected save on1.1.110. It asserts the renamed earned state, native speed modifier, both queues, suspended work, foreign disablement and unrelated mining modifier before fixture writes. One real successor lab completes the partial laser research; independent tool-durability accounting checks35/60 science consumption. Save and two further read-only cold reloads must preserve the completed bytes. The original source and all adverse receipts remain unchanged.

Use the existing governed native runner with its explicit `F100F110LaserStage=source` or `successor` admission. It verifies exact engine/profile/fixture composition and requires the successor profile's protected source hash. No modern observer, historical fixture override, active seed or creation-only mode is admitted. Fixture preparation and host controls do not establish native acceptance.
